The geometry is right, but 'for any cage length' is not. Numbers: T 97.946 (probe_fitfast shape.T), Ls 39.464 (row best_params.Ls), rho 81.83. pointer-cslide.py angles() gives the band arc T + Ls + 2 x deg(3/(rho+2)) = 97.95 + 39.46 + 4.10 = 141.51 deg. The cage walks x/2 while the shoe walks x in [-T/2, T/2]. Take a cage longer than the shoe, Lc = Ls + T/2 = 88.43 deg: then the shoe always sits over cage-held balls. Over the stroke the cage spans Lc + T/2 = T + Ls = 137.41 deg, which is the band arc 141.51 less its two 2.05-deg end stops. The cage reaches the stop face together with the shoe at full stroke. So the declared caged-ball J3 fits the modelled 141.5-deg band unchanged; the row already declares the custom cage and the anti-creep (row mechanism.notes). Unloaded balls ride outside the shoe, as in a ball-retainer telescopic slide. Neither the band nor the claim changes.

Upheld. Measured: the saddle's fitted grid is 14 x 79 per-sample quantile radii, interpolated onto the 14 x 105 sampled columns. It is not steeper than a kit strap: max axial step 2.1 mm per 2 mm (46.3 deg), max circumferential step 2.15 mm per 2.68 mm (38.7 deg), none past the K5 60-deg line (pointer-cslide_skeptic_extra.json saddle_step_*). So steepness does not set it apart from the K3 straps that every kit row uses. Its form does: a doubly-curved underside 26 mm x 141 deg with a body 6.0-31.4 mm thick (saddle_counterfactual band_body_thickness_mm), carrying 1470 of 2585 samples and ~48 in-band points. A K3 strap is a constant 3 mm section that becomes a bent bar.
